gate: H1b-1 Maynard Lemmas 8.1-8.4 basic summation constant audit
scope: Source-level decomposition of the singular-series, Lipschitz, one-dimensional multiplicative summation, and iterated summation constants used in Maynard Lemmas 8.1-8.4. This is not a quantitative reproof and supplies no numerical theorem threshold.

status_vocabulary.PRINTED_STRUCTURAL_FACT: The source explicitly states the structural fact, but this alone is not a numerical summation bound.
status_vocabulary.SOURCE_CHAIN_TRACED: The cited lower-level theorem and specialization are identified, while its implied multiplier remains non-numeric.
status_vocabulary.CONSTRUCTIVE_SUBPROBLEM: A finite choice or inequality can be specified by the project, but has not yet been quantitatively proved and composed.
status_vocabulary.PROJECT_FINITE_COMPONENT_CLOSED: A project proof supplies a finite explicit formula and range for the named component, without closing the parent package.
status_vocabulary.PARAMETERIZED_EXPLICIT: The propagation formula is explicit in a named upstream multiplier, but that upstream multiplier or its finite range is still missing.
status_vocabulary.PARTIAL_EXPLICIT: A finite majorant is explicit after numeric input normalization, but at least one source coefficient or common range remains open.
status_vocabulary.RATE_MISSING: At least one O, o, Vinogradov multiplier, norm, or sufficiently-large cutoff is not numerical.
status_vocabulary.LOWER_SOURCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED: A lower cited proof must be quantitatively reconstructed before a multiplier can be certified.
status_vocabulary.SOURCE_ACCESS_BLOCKED: The exact lower-source pages have been located, but the available legal preview does not expose the proof needed to recover the multiplier.
status_vocabulary.HARD_BLOCKER: The composed basic-summation package cannot be certified until every upstream row has a numerical bound and common range.

obligations.role: small-prime part of the singular-series lower bound
obligations.printed_information: H1b-1a proves product_{p<=2k}(1/p)>exp(-4k); together with the tail this gives S_B(L)>exp(-9k/2) for every integer k>=1.

obligations.role: large-prime tail of the singular-series lower bound
obligations.printed_information: H1b-1a proves the tail product is greater than exp(-k/2), so together with the small-prime part S_B(L)>exp(-9k/2) for every integer k>=1.

obligations.role: average Delta/phi(Delta) estimate for nearby extra linear forms
obligations.printed_information: H1b-1a proves E(k)<24 log(k) and a parameterized finite majorant 72 A_phi Y log(k)+3Y U(M)V(M)/log(Y).
missing_numeric_inputs: numeric A0 and B0 replacing the source Vinogradov input bounds
uniform composition with the permitted k, eta, and x ranges
the common cutoff needed to absorb the second term into the allocated error budget

obligations.role: fully specified smooth cutoff psi and its norms
obligations.printed_information: H1b-1a fixes psi(t)=sigma(10(1-t)) from the standard flat bump and proves sup|psi'|<50.

obligations.role: Lipschitz control for shifted coefficient arguments
obligations.printed_information: H1b-1b proves that the H1b-1a cutoff gives |y_s-y_r| <= 89 T_k Y_r log(A)/log(R) in part (i), and the same multiplier 89 with Y_r+Y_s in part (ii), uniformly for every integer k>=2.

obligations.locator: Maynard Lemma 8.3; GGPY2009 Lemma 4 with kappa=1
obligations.printed_information: Castillo et al. show that under the stated hypotheses the safe base error is absolute, without c_gamma. H1b-1b makes the kappa=1 partial-summation transfer explicit: an absolute Lemma 3 multiplier C3(A1,A2) gives absolute Lemma 4 multiplier 2 C3(A1,A2) for GGPY's norm M(F).
missing_numeric_inputs: the numerical absolute upstream multiplier C3(A1,A2) from the HR/Kuperberg proof chain
the common finite z range inherited from that upstream proof
a uniform lower bound for c_gamma or an explicit stronger z-versus-L gate before converting the absolute error to Maynard's printed relative form

obligations.locator: Maynard published version, note following Lemma 8.3
obligations.role: version-control correction for the general kappa statement
obligations.printed_information: The published paper notes that a c_gamma(L+1)^kappa error is needed in general and says this general-kappa issue does not affect kappa=1. Castillo et al. identify a distinct issue that remains at kappa=1: the c_gamma factor in the error does not follow from the stated hypotheses without an additional z-versus-L size condition.
missing_numeric_inputs: the numerical multiplier still hidden in the kappa=1 absolute error term
the extra condition or c_gamma lower bound needed for the printed relative normalization

obligations.locator: GGPY2009 Lemma 3; Halberstam-Richert Lemmas 5.3-5.4; Kuperberg2023 Lemma 4.3
obligations.role: lower-level summation estimate used by GGPY Lemma 4
obligations.printed_information: GGPY identifies HR Lemmas 5.3-5.4. Kuperberg gives an accessible modern structural reproduction after HR Lemma 5.4 and displays an O((L+k^4)/log z) relative error under implicit B_L and B_k size conditions for a special prime-tuple sieve function. It does not supply project-ready numerical constants or a general Maynard gamma specialization.
missing_numeric_inputs: explicit B_L and B_k and every O multiplier in the Kuperberg/HR recurrence
a checked specialization from the reproduced prime-tuple sieve function to every Maynard Lemma 8.4 gamma
a common finite range and numerical absolute multiplier

obligations.locator: Maynard Lemma 8.4, verification of Lemma 8.3 hypotheses
obligations.role: numerical A1 and A2 for the multiplicative function gamma
obligations.printed_information: The proof has gamma(p)=0 on excluded primes and gamma(p)=1+O(k/p) otherwise, and says fixed A1,A2 are available for sufficiently large k.
missing_numeric_inputs: the O multiplier in gamma(p)=1+O(k/p)
specific admissible values of A1 and A2
the first k for which the hypotheses hold uniformly

obligations.role: prime-divisor discrepancy parameter in repeated summation
obligations.printed_information: The proof bounds L by a constant multiple of log log R after splitting small and large prime divisors.
missing_numeric_inputs: constants in both prime-divisor sums
the hidden exponent in W/product(e_i) <= R^(O(k^2))
a finite R and k range

obligations.printed_information: The error is controlled by r Omega_G log log R/log R times the main scale.
missing_numeric_inputs: a numerical Omega_G after propagating the explicit cutoff norm through the actual k-dependent test function
the constants connecting Omega_G to G_max and the integral
a finite proof of r Omega_G=o(log R/log log R)

obligations.locator: Maynard Lemma 8.4, r-fold application of Lemma 8.3
obligations.role: accumulation and absorption of one-dimensional summation errors
obligations.printed_information: The proof applies Lemma 8.3 repeatedly and replaces products of 1+O(epsilon) by a total O(r epsilon) error.
missing_numeric_inputs: a certified smallness range for epsilon
the exact binomial or exponential accumulation multiplier
a common range after all r iterations
a corrected r-fold derivation because the per-step absolute error does not automatically factor with c_gamma
a uniform c_gamma lower bound or explicit z-versus-L gate at every iteration

obligations.role: single numerical basic-summation package for later moment proofs
obligations.printed_information: The source chain and qualitative error shapes are identified, but no common numerical cutoff or multiplier table is printed.
missing_numeric_inputs: all upstream numerical constants
one explicit cutoff function and norm package
a shared error budget and maximum finite cutoff

parent_ledger_update.reason: The source chain and peer-reviewed error-term correction are traced. Kuperberg supplies an accessible structural HR reproduction, but numerical constants, finite ranges, the c_gamma normalization repair and the r-fold composition remain open.

next_gate.description: Quantitatively reconstruct the Kuperberg/HR recurrence, recover an absolute C3(A1,A2) and finite range, prove either a uniform c_gamma lower bound or an explicit z-versus-L restoration gate, and only then redo the factor-2 transfer and Maynard Lemma 8.4 r-fold composition.
